parameters.content:
## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run: n8n renders the downloaded MP4 as an inline
video player with a download button — today's quote reel, no URL to copy.

*Run summary* before it still carries `videoUrl` (and `jobId`,
`creditsCharged`) if you want to pipe the result onward.

## Daily motivational quote videos from a Google Sheet

Every morning this workflow takes the first quote in your sheet that has not
been used yet, renders it as a polished 1080x1920 quote reel (~11-14 s) with
Zvid, then writes the finished video URL back to that row and marks it done.
The background footage and music rotate daily from a curated pool, so the
channel never posts the same look two days in a row.

### Setup (about three minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **Google Sheets** — attach your Google credential to *Read quote sheet* and
   *Mark row done*, then pick your spreadsheet and tab in both nodes.
   The expected columns are in the yellow note next to the sheet node.
3. **Open `Config`** — set `channelName` and `ctaText` to your brand.
4. **Run it — the first run renders for real and spends about 11 credits.**
   `dryRun` is `false` out of the box. When it finishes, click
   **▶ Watch video** to play the reel right here in n8n.
5. Want a free preview first? Set `dryRun: true` in **Config**: you get the
   credit quote plus an **editorLink** to watch the video in the editor,
   nothing spent and the sheet untouched. Set it back to `false` to render.
6. **Activate** — it posts a fresh quote video to the sheet every day at 8am.

### Cost per video

A ~11 s quote reel is about **11 credits**; a two-hundred-character quote
(~14 s) is about **14**. *Validate project (free)* runs before every render and
reports the figure as `creditsCharged`, but the render then proceeds on its
own — a `dryRun: true` pass gives you the number without spending anything.

## Your sheet: five columns

Header row (row 1), spelled exactly like this:

| Quote | Author | AuthorNote | Status | VideoUrl |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

- **Quote** + **Author** — required. AuthorNote is an optional line under the
  author's name on the end card ("Writer & essayist").
- **Status** — leave EMPTY for quotes waiting to be rendered. The workflow
  takes the first empty-Status row (top to bottom), and writes `done` +
  the video URL when the render finishes. Put anything in Status by hand to
  skip a row.
- Batch-paste a month of quotes whenever you like — one row is consumed per
  day, and when every row is used the workflow simply reports "nothing to
  render" until you add more.

## Why it looks different every day

*Build project JSON* carries a **pool of five curated background clips, each
paired with a music bed** — misty forest, ember ink, rain on a window, a sea
of clouds, a calm shore. The day-of-year picks the entry
(`dayOfYear % 5`), so the rotation is deterministic: no repeats on
consecutive days within a year, and a re-run on the same day produces the same
look. (A leap year ends on day 366 and 366 % 5 == 1 % 5, so that one New Year's
Day repeats New Year's Eve — pin poolIndexOverride if it matters.)
Every URL in the pool was verified reachable when this template was built.

- Pin one look: set `poolIndexOverride` (0-4) in Config.
- Bring your own: `backgroundVideoOverride` / `musicUrlOverride`
  (portrait ~1080x1920, at least 10 s of video).

Type scales with content: the quote drops from 62 px to 42 px as it grows
towards ~220 characters, and long author names shrink to fit the end card —
no clipping, no overflow.

## Free preview: the optional dry run

**`dryRun` is `false` in Config, so a run renders for real.** Set it to
`true` whenever you want a free pass instead: the workflow validates the
payload, quotes the exact credit cost and saves the project as a **draft**,
then reports an **editorLink** like `https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the exact video and tweak anything by hand, with nothing
spent. **The sheet row is not marked done on a dry run**, so the next real
run renders the same quote.

Set `dryRun` back to `false` to render and mark the row done.

## Publishing the video (optional tail)

The workflow ends with the video URL in the sheet — a clean handoff you can
extend after **Mark row done**:

- **YouTube Shorts** — add an *HTTP Request* node (GET the `videoUrl`,
  response format `File`) followed by the native **YouTube** node
  (Video → Upload, binary `data`). Needs a YouTube OAuth2 credential.
- **Instagram / TikTok / everywhere** — pass `videoUrl` to a scheduler
  like Blotato, Buffer or Metricool via their HTTP API; they accept a public
  video URL directly, no download step needed.
- **Human in the loop** — a Slack or Email node that sends `videoUrl` to
  whoever posts manually.

They are left out of the required path on purpose so the template imports
and runs with a Zvid key and a Google account, nothing else.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow runs
anywhere, including n8n Cloud with nothing installed.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit render | **Zvid** → Render → Create |
| Get render status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |
